kestrel_settings._comment_java_memory: 12g is load-bearing. 4g measured +1.2s with CPU rising 3.88x to 7.29x (G1 thrashing), and the KAnalyze count step peaks near 7.7GB at -d16. Do not shrink it because the observed peak RSS of a single run looks smaller.
kestrel_settings._comment_split_counting: Kestrel never configures the KAnalyze CountModule it builds, so counting - roughly 88% of its work - runs one k-mer and one split thread. true runs kanalyze count as its own threaded step and hands Kestrel the resulting IKC. false is an operator kill switch that restores the single-command path exactly; nothing selects it automatically, and a failed count still raises rather than falling back.
kestrel_settings._comment_keep_ikc: Retain the attempt directory and its IKC after the run, for diagnosing a result. Off by default because the IKC is roughly the size of the input k-mer set.
kestrel_settings._comment_java_opts: The count step is genuinely parallel once the thread budget reaches it, so it keeps the G1 default. The call step is single-threaded, where G1 spawns a GC worker per core against one application thread. -XX:+UseParallelGC is harmful on both and must not be used.

subthreshold_note._comment: #266. One banner line on a sample that called nothing but held a candidate failing only the depth gate. It is a note, never a row: summary.parse_tsv routes '#' lines into `comments`, so no consumer of the table can read it as a call. Only the sentence is configurable; the marker it starts with is a machine contract in subthreshold.NOTE_MARKER, because the writer (kestrel_genotyping) and the reader (generate_report) do not load the same config file. Set `enabled` to false to restore the pre-#266 output exactly.
subthreshold_note.template: {marker} {events} {noun} in the pathogenic frame identified below the reporting floor (best Depth_Score {best_depth_score}, floor {floor}); filtered out and NOT a call. Depth_Score is a ratio against an active-region depth summed over the repeat array, so the same alternate k-mer-path depth scores lower on a longer allele.
